utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Forand, before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First matter I want to deal with this morning, General Forand, is the matter you said yesterday evening towards the end of your evidence that you had only received three letters from Mr. Cermak, when I was asking you questions as to why you didn't recognise him as the garrison commander of Knin. Do you recollect that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I think what I said is I thought I had received only three letters. There was not an affirmative that it was only three.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we just look at that issue, because you were putting it as an excuse as to why you didn't recognise his title as the "Zborno Mjesto" of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, over night, we have collected together a bundle of correspondence from Mr. Cermak to General Forand. Mr. Usher, if could you put that there. It is before General Forand, and there are 15 letters from -- in the name of General Cermak to General Forand, one of which is not signed by General Cermak, and we will be looking at that later in the evidence. Now, it hasn't been uploaded into e-court yet obviously, because it was a matter that arose overnight. Some of these letters are duplicates of letters that are already in, but it makes the point in the collection. I'm really seeking Your Honour's guidance or direction as to how the Court wants to deal with the issue in this way. We have put it together as a collection to make a simple point, without making it too complicated and going through each letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest the following, Mr. Tieger, and please let me know whether you would agree with that: That a list of letters which are not yet in evidence, the letters attached to that list, and then adding to that list the details of letters that are already in evidence, and then to tender this from the bar table and give Mr. Forand an opportunity to read these letters over the break and then perhaps answer questions as to whether he has received those letters or whatever comment he has in relation to the letters now presented to him, in view of his testimony of yesterday. Would that be practical solution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I may not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone is not on, but I will switch mean off then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Same problem, Your Honour. I think it is blinking and not -- okay. Your Honour, thank you. It seems to be a practical solution. One issue occurs to me, and that is that if the documents are going to be shown to the witness as documents which he may or may not have received, it is probably helpful to identify which of the documents are translations conducted here rather than documents he would have received at the time. I see there are a lot of English documents which we recognise as being translations of B/C/S documents but which the witness may not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would consider this to be among the questions that will be put to him once he has had an opportunity to read them. Mr. Forand, we're more or less now claiming one of your next breaks, instead of having a cup of coffee, to just go through this bundle of letters and to see to what extent you recognise the content or whether remember to have seen them. Would that be okay, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Kay, if you would prepare that list for later filing, and if we leave now a bundle with Mr. Forand, and then I take it that after the break you put the questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sometimes, General, this issues can be taken quite shortly, and I will just ask you in view of the fact I haven't been typing these overnight, but I got them obviously from a collection which the Prosecution had whether you would like to revise your testimony of yesterday? I'm just giving an opportunity over that issue.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously, you know, just looking at the first one, all the letters that were addressed to me I should have received. I didn't remember them. I based my comment yesterday on what I had seen in the folder that I was provided, which had, if I remember well, only three letters. But I'm sure that all the letters that General Cermak wrote to me I received, you know, either personally or through my Senior Liaison Officer. I have no problem with that. The comment you made, when I said yesterday, it was not the only reason, you know, that it was three letters. It was the fact that in all of letters that I sent to General Cermak, it was addressed as the military commander and he never made allusions or told me that that was not his right title.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A bit like always addressing someone with the wrong name, whether you tell them you've got my name wrong.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's then look at what this position was. First document we're going to look at it is D31, an exhibit previously produced in the trial. This is a document dated the 5th of August and concerns the appointment by the president of Croatia of General Cermak to be the commander of the Knin garrison. Can you see that, General Forand?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the previous holder of that position of commander of the Knin garrison was Major Gojevic, who became the deputy commander. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now, this document was issued on the 5th of August and concerns General Cermak's appointment to that position that I told you he held rather than military governor. And "ZM" that you saw on the letters from General Cermak to you stand for "Zborno Mjesto," commander of the garrison. So there you can see that that was his official appointment?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw that letter personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. When you were in Knin, you had a press office. Did you receive information from the press officer about matters of interest that were happening in relation to Croatian policy in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The press officer that was there was not under my responsibility. He was working for UNCRO headquarter. And, obviously, if there was something of interest, he was assisting, if I remember well, at our 8.30 meeting, so he would pass it on to everybody at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we look at a newspaper article that came out on the 6th of August, D36.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit D36, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This newspaper report of the next day from a paper called Slobodna Dalmacija, which will shortly be on your screen, again is a public statement in the press about General Cermak's appointment on the 5th of August. And in the translation there, you will see that that appointment was to be commander of the Knin garrison, and Major Gojevic, the deputy commander, having previously been the commander. Gojevic you knew to be General Cermak's deputy. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that Major Gojevic -- I don't remember that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Didn't you meet him on the 5th of September with General Gotovina at the meeting when you went to the quarters, the new office of General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Didn't you have dealings with Major Gojevic as General Cermak's deputy?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that individual at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. You can see there in this article General Cermak, during 1990 to 1991, was an advisor to the president; then an assistant minister of defence; and, in 1993, minister of economy in the government of Croatia. Did you appreciate that until his appointment on the 5th of August, that General Cermak was actually in civilian life, he wasn't a serving army officer?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not at that time, because I don't remember ever seeing that article or I don't remember being briefed, you know, on that particular article. But as I said yesterday, maybe three weeks afterwards, there was a social function where we had exchanged a few words, and he told me that he was a reserve officer at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know that he was a civilian, in fact, until appointed on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly if he was a civilian up to the 5th, but I remember he told me that he was a businessman, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Did you think he was a serving army officer at that time that he was a military man?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because he had told me he was a reserve officer. That's why yesterday when you told me at that time that he was the - I don't know if could call him like that - the mastermind of the artillery plan. To me, in myself, I did not believe him and I never passed that information to anybody, expect I think I passed it on when I was interviewed by the ICTY people because they were asking me, you know, what I thought about General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And there's an issue between us over your account on that matter, as you appreciate, because I suggest to you he had insufficient knowledge of the English language to give you that information in a conversation.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I remember that we don't agree on that. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any knowledge of the structure of the Croatian armed forces at that time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I still don't today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you were unaware of the responsibilities of the person that you were dealing with. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, unaware in the sense of his overall responsibility; aware of the fact that he told me that he was responsible for the Knin region which corresponds to my sector of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it that you thought he was responsible for the area over which you had command because that is the terms in which you were thinking?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly thought that he was responsible because I had been told by General Gotovina, when I had raised with him the looting and the burning and the conduct of the military personnel, to refer those matter to General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Should we just have a look at that statement that you just made there, because if we go to Exhibit 359, the meeting on the 8th of August, and it's page 3 of that sitrep, you can see there the report of the meeting that you had with General Gotovina. And nowhere in that report is there any statement that you raised the issue of crimes with General Gotovina, crimes by the Croatian army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's not there. But in the supplementary that was deposited yesterday by the Prosecutor, I said that I recall that I had a discussion with General Gotovina, but it does not appear, you're right, on that sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What this sitrep shows is that, in fact, you did very little talking at all. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's sole reference to what you say was asking permission to bring your COs to Knin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, because at that time, you know, we still could not get out of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now, when you went to Gotovina, to see General Gotovina on the 8th of August, you were just raising matters that were of concern to the UN, weren't you, to you as commander, Sector South, UNCRO?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was my only responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The issue of crimes being committed was not something that you had gone to see General Gotovina about.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because he is the one who invited me to visit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly. So he was speaking to you and was telling you what the situation was going to be as between Croatia, which was now in occupation of its own territory, and you, as the UNCRO commander, who was on their territory. That's what that meeting was about, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly those --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You weren't there raising issues with General Gotovina outside your own concerns of getting UNCRO out of Croatia. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would assume, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, in fact, when you were interviewed in 1996, 1997, 1998 -- 1999, sorry, you never mentioned that you went to see General Gotovina on the 8th of August and discussed crimes being committed at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This might not rise as a general matter, because I think it is significant here, I think the witness should be pointed to those passages of the particular statements where that -- I mean, either to review the statements in their entirety or to be pointed to the passages where that meeting is referenced, because I think it would be pertinent here. And I don't say anything more at this time in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can do it this a long way, Your Honour, and time is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that. At the same time, Mr. Kay, I noticed, and I will address that, that the witness is -- I will say one word about that. There are other matters such as how Mr. Cermak was appointed, where the witness can hardly add anything, where you really take your time to put quite a lot of things to the witness. So I do understand that time is important it is, however, a matter of how to use the time, what to prioritise. And I can imagine that, in view of what I just heard, that it makes some sense to briefly take him through these statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Forand, I noticed the following: On the last few questions about what was raised and what was the subject of this meeting, you more or less followed what Mr. Kay suggested to you. At the same time, earlier today, you said, talking about the sitrep, "Yeah, it is not there. But in the supplementary that was deposited yesterday," you said that you recall having a discussion with -- no, no. I have to withdraw that. Please try to listen very carefully to what Mr. Kay puts to you and try to focus on whether you agree with him or not, try to be very price in these matters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I certainly don't want to make this more cumbersome and lengthy than necessary. Is it helpful if I draw Mr. Kay's attention to one particular --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm going to cut it short in view of the way the intervention occurred, and I was astonished by the intervention because we go to the statement in 2008, Exhibit P333.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And in 2008, for the first time, you mention that on the 8th of August, you complained to General Gotovina about the lack of discipline of his troops. They were looting and burning in the town, and then you say: "General Gotovina referred me to General Cermak for these and any other complaints."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do need some guidance, Your Honour. I hear comments from counsel that I should do this in redirect. But if the witness is being lead to a portion of his statement in what appears to be a conflation of two issues that suggest something that to him that is not fair, I feel I should rise and try to ensure that it is addressed clearly before redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you should wait, Mr. Tieger. At the same time, Mr. Kay, what I did before is I have drawn the witness's attention that where he, at one moment, says that the issue of crimes has been raised and that he in his last statement -- didn't say in the sitrep nothing is there, but in his last statement he said something about it, if then at a later stage he says, Well, following your suggestions what the subject was, that we might lack precision there. At the same time, it is perfectly fair if you put to the witness, and I think we can do it in such a way at this moment, that you, Mr. Kay, see, for the first time, that the witness raises the issue during his last interview. I also mention to you that -- I draw your attention to the fact that most important is whether the recollection of the witness is firm in this respect. And, of course, you can put questions to him, Why didn't you say this any earlier. But, finally, what important is whether his recollection is firm on that; and, of course, you can explore where he didn't say it earlier or that his recollection is not firm on that. Mr. Forand, I take it that you followed some of the discussions. Mr. Kay showed that he was a bit surprised that issues were raised only recently in your last statement, and he would like to ask you some questions about that. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, how did it come about that you recalled it here in 2008, 12 years later, and didn't recall it earlier?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because obviously, you know, I was preparing myself to come and be a witness here; and the more I read, you know, what I had put in my presentation and the more I thought about it, I realised, you know, that I had spoken those words to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it suggested to you in any way that this was a subject that was raised? Was it suggested to you by anyone?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, there it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I want it look at exhibit 65 ter 4028, which is a presidential transcript of President Tudjman, and if on that document we can go to 03049095, which is page 20 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This, again, is from the Prosecution documents and is part of a discussion in the president's office with various people - Ivo Sanadar, Mr. Zuzul, others - concerning the Canadians. And a reference in the middle of the page by Mr. Zuzul, the Canadians: The Americans received an official request to assist the Canadians in pulling out of Knin. This transcript dates from the 7th of August, 1995. Is that right that there was assistance sought by the Canadians to pull out of Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard about that one, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you can see below that the president says: "And another thing, tell them I appointed as commander of the Knin garrison Colonel-General Cermak, a former minister, a serious man to solve those matters." Again, from the president not saying that General Cermak was a military governor but he was commander of the Knin garrison. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, but I never saw that document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: All right. And that's what General Cermak had told you, wasn't it, that he was there to help you as commander of Sector South in the problems that you had ending your mission. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember those exact words, but we were to discuss with him and to work with him, you know, if any problem arise, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it wasn't a matter that he had command over the same area that was your area, Sector South. He never said that to you.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. What I remember is that he told me that he was the individual responsible for the Knin region, which, in my view, was my whole area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, to be fair to you, you were looking at it from your perspective?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember, sir, which perspective I should had been looking then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can make that extract an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D296.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, may I take it that there is no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D296 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know that there had been discussions about help and that you wanted to see General Cermak, between other international politicians, representatives, and the president's office in Zagreb, about the help you needed to withdraw from the region?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about. I never heard about that one either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, did you know that, in fact, the president's advisor, one of his special advisor, Mr. Sarinic, who signed the agreement with Mr. Akashi, in relation to your problems stated that Mr. Cermak was the "koschnik" of Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard about that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. Did you know at the time who a man called "koschnik" was and what he did?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A man who was appointed as the administrator of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: To revitalize the city there and to bring the parties together in Mostar. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When Mr. Cermak came to Knin, you met him on the 7th of August, when Mr. Akashi came to your camp. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And at Exhibit D29, we can see the report that was filed by Mr. Akashi of what Mr. Cermak said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that up on the screen? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at page 1 of that report, one can see that Mr. Cermak was concerned with restoring water and electricity and about the removal of HV troops. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you agree with that as well, in your dealings with him, on that day --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- of the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly if it was discussed on the 7th at that particular meeting, because I had a subsequent meeting, you know, in the evening with him. Yes. I believe that he told me that his responsibility was to restore normal life, you know, as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And on that 7th of August, if we look at page 2 of Mr. Akashi's report, at paragraph 4, he was professing a strong desire for all those people still in Knin in your camp to remain living there and not to leave the region. Do you recollect that those were the statements that he was making at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly at that time, but I know that he made that statement to the refugee themselves, I think, the following days. But at that particular meeting, I don't remember. But if Mr. Akashi remember, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I don't want to have to show a film, as my time is limited, but we have a film of him saying this, that the --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I agree, you know, because I remember that he had said that to the refugee themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Straight away, would you agree, when he got in that camp, he was pledging support to try and sort out that problem that the UN was dealing with?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And straight away, he was making statements that damage would be repaired and that these people should stay and be allowed to live freely and without hindrance. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: All his statements on that day were publicly supportive of trying to resolve, peaceably and amicably, the problem that was within your UN camp of the displaced persons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Like I said, I don't remember at that particular meeting; but that meeting at night and subsequent meeting, those words were proffered by General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, for your planning, I inform you that we'll have an earlier break of the first session; that is, quarter past 10.00. There are some urgent matters I have to deal with, and that has to be done at that time. I just inform you so that in your organisation of your cross-examination, that you know that we'll have a break 15 minutes earlier. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. Just dealing with the issue of the military governor, coming back to that, if we could look at a document, P330, Exhibit P330 -- oh, no, sorry. That's the statement. My mistake. It's P347, Exhibit P347.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was your letter on the 5th of August requesting a meeting with the military governor and sent to General Gotovina, saying you urgently request a meeting, as there are a number of issues concerning the displaced persons: "There has been a significant amount of destruction and looting. I'm not satisfied the Croatian army is fully under control," and referring to freedom of movement. At what time on the 5th of August did you issue this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. If we turn to 65 ter 1977, this document is "Points to be discussed with military governor, HV commanders, UN operations," and it's got written on it: "Copy given to Captain Lukovic, 6th of August," at 10.00. Was this a document drafted by you or someone in your office?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to see what date was it produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It says: "Copy given to Captain Lukovic 6th, Aug 1995, 1000 hours."

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But on the opposite there, it seems to indicate the 11th of kolizar -- kolivaz [phoen]. Is that August?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's August.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't make sense, you know, if it was produced on the 11th, that we had given it on the 6th. I don't know who wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where do you see the 11th?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my screen, just to the right of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Forget the one on the right there.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the one I'm looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's not the same --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- document. Yeah, forget that. Look at the English -- no. We've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we now moved to the worse; that is, where we would expect to have a B/C/S translation to the right of the document, we find on the left. Then the next step was that we now had the wrong document in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just look at the left-hand side. This is an English written document rather than a translation.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Points to be discussed with the military governor. Was that a document written by you, drafted by you, or any hand that you had in it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not drafted by me, but the points that needed to be discussed had been identified by me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, there seems to be, however, a problem not necessarily caused by you, but that document that was just on the right of the screen is the translation attached to this document, and apparently is not the translation of this document. So there must be a wrong attachment. If it was a document that was uploaded by the Prosecution, you're invited, Mr. Tieger, to check that, because what appears to the B/C/S translation is, at least what is attached as the B/C/S translation, certainly is not a translation of that document. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, it is not one of mine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason why I'm addressing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document and is it a document that you took with you for your meeting on the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recognise the document because it's a situation report. I don't have the date that it was written. I didn't bring the situation report with me because it was written after the meeting. But obviously the points, you know, that are highlighted there are points that I wanted to discuss or have discussed in that situation report with General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can that document be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And, of course, I understand the issue with the translation and will attend to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we assign a number to the English original, which is ERN number 00901522. This will be admitted into evidence, but the Prosecution should report on uploading a proper translation of this document. Mr. Registrar, it would be admitted under number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D297, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D297 with the proviso I just expressed is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, can we look at P348, Exhibit 348.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a sitrep of the 6th of August, released by you. We only need to look at the first page and paragraph 1, where you have concerns with the current situation in Knin and Sector South: "I will be discussing those points at my level with the Croat liaison office in Knin; however, I would appreciate if those points were discussed with Croat authorities in Zagreb." What was the level you were referring to as the Croat liaison office in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, it was at Captain Lukovic level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He's the naval officer we mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the one that I met a couple of times, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And also referred to on the points to be discussed document in handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is what was written, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You gave him a copy of that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must have. I don't remember exactly, because in those days we were discussing that Captain Lukovic would take a position within my headquarters. That was the initial discussion that had taken place, and I don't remember the reason why it then came to. But we never had the liaison -- Croat liaison officer within my headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did it come about, in fact, that you had one of your UN liaison officers within Mr. Cermak's offices in Knin, the garrison HQ?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear. I don't remember exactly if we tried to have one and for whatever reason it didn't work, but my Senior Liaison Officer, Lieutenant-Colonel Tymchuk, went there on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. He was within the office area of General Cermak in Knin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think he had a place, you know, permanently there, but he was going on a daily basis to visit the office of General Cermak. Not always with General Cermak, I think with his staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can ask him about that. In this document here, that you appreciate it if these points were discussed with Croat authorities in Zagreb, what did you have in mind or what was the position in relation to discussion in Zagreb? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean my headquarters, UNCRO headquarters, with their counterpart on the Croat authority, to discuss the point that I would be raising. At that time, what you have shown me before now, I have some recollection. It was not part of a situation report, but it was a list of points that I wanted to address, to whoever was in charge in the Knin area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And at that time, the only contact I had was with Captain Lukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. In relation to what you told us yesterday about what you had seen, the crimes, problems that you had, were those problems also matters that you were referring up your chain of command to the headquarters in Zagreb? Were they aware of what you were dealing with?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, because on every situation report that I was making daily, and sometime more than one time a day, a situation report describing the situation within all of my area of responsibility on a daily basis to my headquarters at UNCRO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of sending it to the HQ in Zagreb? What was the action to be taken from there?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a normal way of doing business in the military, where you report the situation on a daily basis; and, hopefully, you know, if it's something requesting intervention, I was hoping, you know, that they would do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the information that you were giving them from Knin passed up the command to Zagreb was information that you were expecting them to deal with, as well, to help your problems. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In certain case, not all the case, the other case was reporting what we were seeing. And in some certain instances, it was a specific request that was included in the sitrep asking them to take action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And we haven't heard evidence about this yet, but the system that was in play with the headquarters in Zagreb and the information that was going back to the command in Zagreb that was information and facts that they could deal with themselves. You weren't the only person having to deal with the problems in Knin, would that be right, on a global level, or an overall picture?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at UNCRO itself, I was the only organisation reporting to my headquarters. The UN civil police were reporting to their own organisation, and they belong to UNPROFOR. The human rights people also were a different route. The military observers also was a different route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday you weren't responsible for those other organisations.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They reported to separate headquarters in Zagreb. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And the majority of the time, I could not vouch all the time, but the majority of the time we were receiving an information copy of what they were sending to their responsible organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. And having informed the headquarters in Zagreb, the matters of which you were complaining of, were matters that your superiors could deal with in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was hoping, yes, that they could be dealing with it, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And when you're reporting about crimes, that they can take it at a higher level from you to a higher level than the local level to the officers with which they worked in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I just now want to turn to something that you raised of Mr. Cermak telling you about the normalization of life in Knin as being something with which he was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to a document which I have, 2D03-0085.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have a letter dated the 8th of August which is also in that collection we produced earlier this morning, General Forand, which is from General Cermak to you in which he mentioned in order to return normal life an order in Knin and open up and restore traffic. Was this a letter that was received by you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must have received that. I don't remember. But like I said earlier, every letter that General Cermak addressed to me, I have to have received it at my headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was an established system --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- between you --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- through the liaison officers. And you agree that when you met General Cermak that he told you that that was one of his tasks, was to normalize life in Knin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. But I thought it was more in Knin but also the region of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And to revitalize and get business going within Knin, was that a subject that he raised with you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the business part, but I remember that he mentioned many times that he wanted the activity to return to normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And he was writing a letter such as this to you, which reflected conversations that you had had with him in meetings between each other. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been. I don't remember exactly, but it must have been part of the conversation. I remember sending a letter - I don't know if it is in response to that - saying that we have provided help. And if some of my equipment that had been stolen would have been able, I could do more also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, we're going to look at that in some detail and the paper trail of those letters in a moment, General Forand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we look at the next document, P388, Exhibit P388.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is another document written by him to you on that day, of the 8th of August, referring to the refugees in your camp. And he wanted to address their problems, to see that passes are issued to all who want to leave the camp and go on living in the area of Knin. He wrote: "We will provide all of the conditions of normal life for them," and then refers to drawing up a list. Just dealing with page 1, first of all, again that was very consistent with his statements to you at the meetings about wanting to help all the people inside your UNCRO compound. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that was, in fact, a major problem that you had on your hands at that time to deal with.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the people within my camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it was an unexpected problem for you. On the 3rd of August, you would not anticipated you would be dealing with such a situation.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It was something that you were not prepared for within the camp to have to provide for?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the camp was not suited to have that many people to be taking care of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. On page 2 of this document - and we'll be returning to it later, but just so that it's covered - the question of interviewing men between the ages of 18 and 60 was a matter that was provided for within the Akashi-Sarinic agreement, as to the relationship between the UN and the Croatian authorities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but what the letter -- not the letter but the report that you showed early from Mr. Akashi discussed that it was matter that would have to be further developed because there seemed to be a problem in the way that the interview would be conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The Court has seen the document earlier, and I'm just referencing it here as it is part of this correspondence that has been previously exhibited, the Akashi-Sarinic agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kay, could you give the numbers so that we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not so good with numbers as I used to be when I was younger, and we've had -- I hate to say it, but I'm always needing help on that thing, and it is my own number which makes it even worse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For us to have a look it, we need a P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I do appreciate it. Someone will hopefully provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm told by Mr. Du-Toit that it is D28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. That is the safe way, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not to take credit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Du-Toit. We know that that provision is within that particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can confirm that it is D28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Next document I want to look at is a document 2D03-0087, dated the 8th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's a document, we'll see, where Mr. Cermak, writing the third letter on that day, requests your help with repairing the waterworks in Knin with the aim of normalizing life and work and the return of refugees, considering it was damaged during combat operations. Do you recollect receiving that? It is, in fact, in that little bundle that will you have got.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, I have received it. I don't remember it, but I remember that in the sitrep we talk about the fact that we provided that help to General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Again, part of your joint discussions of working together on these issues to try and get normal life to Knin after the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say it was advantageous to me also because I needed water for my camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May we admit that document as an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Tieger? Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D298 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm reminded I did not ask for 2D03-0085 to be admitted as an exhibit. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are very good at numbers apparently, Mr. Kay. What was it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Good at reading Post-Its.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was document of restoring normal life and work in the town of Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D299, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D299 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at the document 65 ter 3221.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When it comes up on the screen, General Forand, it's a document from General Cermak dated the 9th of August called, "an information," in which General Cermak made a statement to establish trust and continued coexistence in the liberated territory: "We hereby inform all the population of Knin that has fled that the follow is guaranteed to them," and then a number of very important rights. Was that a document that you saw at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that General Cermak went to the camp on several occasions to meet a committee of the internally displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that was all with a view, discussions were taking place because he was working to assure them that they would be safe in the region and that they would have rights, liberties, homes, security, matters that we can see in this list?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not privy to those discussions, but I remember that General Cermak, when he was coming to talk to the displaced persons committee, that was to address those particular points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And I have no need to go any further into that matter. May that be admitted into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D300, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D300 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can just look at one last document before the break at quarter past, it is Prosecution 65 ter 3256, now Prosecution Exhibit 389.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's a letter that you wrote on the 9th of August to General Cermak concerning the UN equipment referring to various matters, and again at the end, saying your staff would like to, again, take up residence in Knin and contribute to the normalization of life. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. What I see is him complaining about the fact that they had cleaned their accommodation, and they went back and again it had been broken into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. There is no issue between us, General Forand, that crimes were being committed. Can I make that entirely clear?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm dealing with particular matters here concerning General Cermak's defence. But both you and he knew in your meetings, as between him and you, that that was the intent, was to normalize life in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he was not excluding any particular people or ethnic group from what he wanted.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what he was telling me, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will look at other issues after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But that is a convenient moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break, and we will resume at 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Kay, the Chamber briefly discussed during the break the course of this cross-examination, and wondered to what extent some of the issues raised are in dispute. Mr. Tieger, for example, from what we see from the letters, the prominent role Mr. Cermak may have played in the restoration of water supply, et cetera, is that an issue or are we just testing whether the witness was aware of all that, which seems to be of very relative relevance?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With respect to the precise question the Court asked me, no, that doesn't seem to be an issue. I can imagine that in certain circumstances, those generic issues may give rise to some contention that then becomes in dispute. But, no, I think, as a general matter, then the Court's impression about that is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So a lot of these, I would say, are civilian affairs, how to get abandoned cars or destroyed cars from the streets and where to leave them. Mr. Kay, if these matters are not in dispute, of course I see that there's an interest of the Cermak Defence to give weight to that, whether the best and the most appropriate way of doing that is to put it to the witness, who then reads the letters and say may I have received them, could be, could not be. Apparently, the witness when he gave his statements was not focussing on these kind of matters, which does not mean that this was not part of reality at the time as well. The main question is whether how to present those elements in such a way that the Chamber becomes fully aware of it, and it might be that testing the awareness of this witness about it might not be the most efficient way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take the indication from the Court. If I may just be permitted to say that we are building a defence and that takes time. We are working in a system where the statement of the witness goes in, in evidence, in great detail, not from an investigating judge but from OTP investigators and others and, as we would say, doesn't create the whole picture available. We were concerned that he had only seen three letters, apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And they were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming you for the three letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was focussing on other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then again if you say this witness doesn't give the complete picture, I think, as a matter of fact, that there is no claim that the statement of the witness gave the complete picture of how Mr. Cermak performed all of his duties, and mainly focussed on what appears to the focus of the Prosecution here. I'm not -- I'm not making jokes, but whether he cared well for his family is also a part of a person, whether he cared well about his duties which were primarily focussing on the well being, the welfare of the those remaining in the city, seems to be not that much in dispute. And, therefore, there might be other ways of completing the picture. Whereas, at this moment, the Prosecution has taken a portion of reality and says this is relevant, primarily relevant, for our case, and to some extent rightly so, because whether he was perfect in restoring the water supply is of limited relevance. I'm not there's saying no relevance, but it is of limited relevance for the charges brought against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. If you want to add, fine; but, otherwise, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I take Your Honours' points. In fact, I've come to the end of this section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I should have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... no. There was just two questions further to ask that had been raised to me that I overlooked, and we were moving on to more mainstream issues. But how someone spends their time in what they do is relevant to the case, in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I earlier said, things are not irrelevant but are of limited relevance compared to other aspects of the case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're going on to deal with other matters soon, General Forand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could we look at a document, which the Defence submit as 2D03-0010.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it is just continuing from the relationship between Mr. Cermak and the people in the camp. I bring it to your attention because allegations are made in this case that there is a certificate there on the 15th of August from a man called Branko Pupavac, who was head of the refugees committee of Sector South camp. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you seen another document similar to this?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I receive one from them, the committee, and named all of the displaced people, but it is not this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you received a similar acknowledgment, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you know Branko Pupavac who was head of the refugees committee?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was one. I don't remember his name, but there was an individual with whom I was speaking once in a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there it is, and thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could that document be admitted, Your Honour, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. D301 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're now going to deal with issues of command or control by General Cermak on the ground. And it's right, is it not, we've seen it in a document exhibited as P361, at page 3, at page 3, in which you have written here: "General Cermak claims total authority other the area of Sector South and grants freedom of movement, but HV units in CanBat 1 area of responsibility, in particular Benkovac, deny General Cermak's authority and even his existence." Can you see that? It is in the middle of the second page.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This document has been duplicated in the system again, and I've referred to a wrong 65 ter that it came under.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But it's page 2, and my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But it is P361 in the middle of the page, under C, fourth line?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And I think it's -- this is a sitrep that you saw. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And was that a problem for you in relation to the denial on the ground of General Cermak's authority, he having issued passes to the UN to freely move in the area?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Well, it was an issue. We were told that we could travel freely --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- with that pass that had been provided, and that was not the case. So, yes, it was creating an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. So you were put on notice that there was a denial of General Cermak's authority or even his existence?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the -- on that sitrep which covers the 8th to the 9th of August, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Did you discuss that with him, as to the denial of his authority?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been raised because it was a problem, you know, that we were facing. So I'm sure that I raised it with him, but I don't remember clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred, in a document yesterday, to him referring to his area of responsibility as being vast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we look at a document that is a report of the same meeting, on the 24th of August, to see how that was expressed. The document that I'd like to look at is Exhibit D151, and it's page 2 of that document in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's the last five lines, and it's a meeting at which Mr. Al-Alfi was present, as well as you and a number of other people. And the record made here is that General Cermak made it clear that: "In his opinion, the area is very vast and he would be lying if he told us nothing of this sort would continue to happen," and it goes on to referring to the issuing of orders. In your record, it says his area of responsibility is vast. Do you see the different meaning from "area" and "area of responsibility"?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say that area of responsibility is more clear than just area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As a military expression, would be -- would that be the way you would contextualize the phrase in this situation, even if he had said "the area is vast"?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my army, we say area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. And so that could be interpreted even if he had said "area" in that form. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We're now going to turn to those missing UN vehicles which deal with an issue concerning what power he had. And we can take the position from a -- first of all, because I want it deal with all the documents relating to this as it's a chain of documents, with a document called 2D03-0089 of the 8th of August. And it's an internal memo to you from someone called Mr. Hoey: "UN vehicles in the hands of the ..." and he's called it HVO. Do you recognise this as something that came to you concerning three documents that were stolen?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but it was addressed to me so I must have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And this started a chain of issues concerning the UN property that was being stolen, and that you asked General Cermak to get back. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go to the next document, which is 65 ter 3220. And may we admit the last document into evidence, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections from the Prosecution. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D302, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D302 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at 3220, you reported to General Cermak, didn't you, about the missing vehicles and wanted him to get them back. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we see here an order that he issued to the military police and Knin police to find those three vehicles on the 9th of August. And that, no doubt, was something that you wanted him to do?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we next look at a document on the -- can we admitted that into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D303, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D303 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document I'd like to call up is exhibit 65 ter 867.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, would it be right to say that you got no report back from General Cermak that the police or military police had found those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly. On the 12th of August, this document shows that General Cermak reported to the Split Military District, command, Chief of Staff: "On several occasions, General Forand, commander of UNCRO forces, has informed us of inappropriate behaviour on the part of the Croatian army." It refers to several vehicles stolen, engineering equipment, and the vehicles have been seen re-painted. Referring to the fact that he had made several attempts without success, and requesting that that officer assist in informing Croatian army unit commanders in the Split Military District of a need to urgently return the equipment and prevent similar acts occurring?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I understand the problem from yesterday because I was reading from a hard copy document and not simultaneously aware that what was being read from not what was tracking on the screen and not available to the witness or the -- or other parties. The first part of the document was, for Mr. Kay's information, as he continued to read, we couldn't see what was in the document on screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The part starting: "As we have attempted on several occasions," was not completely shown on the screen. Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 2, yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, General. I'm unable to exactly see because of all obstructions with what you see. You can take it from me, I'm not making this up. I'm telling you as it is. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, presumably, those are steps that you wanted General Cermak to take?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you note, though, that he is unable to issue such orders to other commanders in the Croatian army in the Military District for the recovery of this property?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seems to be the case. I don't know the Chief of Staff. Who is that Chief of Staff, at what level is it addressed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Chief of Staff was General Ademi?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we go to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May we admit that into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D304, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D304 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to 65 ter 2060.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document issued on the 13th of August, 1995, by the commander of the Split Military District, General Gotovina. Page 1 there refers to the report - this is an unrevised translation - regarding the theft of the vehicles. And you see that an order was issued to the commanders requiring their return, damaging the state interests of the Republic of Croatia, strict disciplinary and other legal measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: All commanders to be informed about this order. And you can see that it is forwarded to all those brigades, battalions, companies, and logistic bases as an order concerning your property. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And do you note that General Cermak didn't have the power to issue it to those divisions within the Split Military District?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That seemed to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May that be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D305, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D305 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And in those list of people to whom the order was referred to, the Knin garrison is not even included. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to exhibit 65 ter 5034.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is an order - when it comes up on the screen - that was issued by one of those commanders in the Split Military District concerning your vehicles and your property, dated the 13th of August. It refers to the previous order issued. It refers to the stealing of vehicles, inappropriate harmful conduct, and then we can see the terms of the order on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And then how it goes through the system from the operations group commander, Colonel Kotomanovic, and to whom it is to be delivered to, those particular regiments and brigades. Again, do you notice that this is not a document from the Knin garrison, the Zborno Mjesto, General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or from any order from him, but within the command of the Split Military District?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can that document be admitted in into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D306 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we turn to Prosecution Exhibit 389.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A document produced yesterday, written by you, General Forand, to Colonel Cermak. And the second paragraph is what we're concerned with on this issue, the second sentence, about: "Is there any progress on locating the three UN vehicles taken from the garage in Knin while being repaired? I would appreciate more timely information on freedom of movement." You wanted information, as you told us yesterday, from General Cermak, as to that was happening on this issue. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you notice from the chains of command, though, that General Cermak was not within those particular units that were passed this order to deal with?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what you've shown me, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Did you appreciate that General Cermak did not, in fact, have the position within the structure of the Split Military District to deal with these issues for you? Did you appreciate that at that time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, no, sir. But based on what you've shown me, obviously, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn now to a document dated the 26th of August, P375, Prosecution Exhibit 375.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it's another letter that you wrote which we looked at yesterday dated the 26th of August, and it's a letter that you wrote to General Gotovina. The first sentence starts: "As discussed in our meting on the 8th August," that's the Knin castle meeting that I have already asked questions to you about this morning. You recollect that, General Forand?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "I'm working in concert with the military governor of Knin, General Cermak, to conclude the UNCRO mission in Sector South and to return units to their home nations." You refer to a number of issues. And on that page, we see that there are increasing number of hostile acts being carried out by Croatian army soldiers against UN peacekeepers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's go to page 2, the paragraph beginning: "On the second issue."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "While I am pleased with the level of cooperation that General Cermak has shown, I am sure that he is very frustrated to find that his authority is limited in certain areas. I cannot understand how joint investigations by UN and Croatian military police can be denied access by junior Croatian army officers to areas that both our military police believe contain UN equipments," and then you refer to Drnis and the compound in Drnis. And it's on this issue of authority that I'm now going to ask you, as I have: Would it be correct to say that you began to realise that General Cermak did not have authority over those Croatian army troops who were in that region?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that what I was thinking in those days that I was finding it very difficult to understand that since he was responsible for the whole Knin region, that when he was telling us that he was taking care, you know, of things that we were advising him was happening, that it didn't seem to have no impact at all. So, yes, I was questioning what is his authority, based on what he is telling me and the problem that we were encountering, you know, as we were moving throughout our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As we see, you were pleased with the level of cooperation. Would it be right to say that you had a good working relationship with him?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. Every meeting that I had with General Cermak, you know, they were cordial, civilised. The only thing that bothered me is that all the problems that we brought to him, nothing seems to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it is continuously referred in my letter to him. But the meeting were very good. I mean, we had never had any shouting match. It was very cordial, very civilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: His door was always open to you. Would that be a fair expression to say?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I would say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you were welcome to go to his office in the garrison command in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had any problem. Every time we asked for an appointment, we had the appointment. And the same for him when he asked to meet with us, there was never any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
